# hamsterd and lemmingd

> Two focused HTTP/HTTPS development proxies written in Go. hamsterd downloads eligible public artifacts once and reuses them across builds or development machines. lemmingd routes selected paths of a real site to local services or alternate hosting origins under the real HTTPS URL.

Project: https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd
License: MIT

## Start here

- [Project overview](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/README.md): installation, building, security, and development commands
- [hamsterd guide](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/docs/hamsterd.md): cache behavior, configuration, supported HTTP semantics, and troubleshooting
- [Terragrunt cache example](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/docs/hamsterd.howto.md): copy-paste workflow for caching Terraform Registry and HashiCorp release downloads
- [lemmingd guide](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/docs/lemmingd.md): route selected domains and paths to local or alternate origins, and launch an isolated configured Firefox profile
- [lemmingd static-site example](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/docs/lemmingd.howto.md): replace remote site assets with locally modified content
- [CA installation](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/docs/ca-installation.md): trust the generated development CA in browsers and command-line clients
- [Security policy](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/SECURITY.md): threat model and vulnerability reporting
- [Example configurations](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/tree/main/examples): ready-to-edit JSON configurations, including an anonymized multi-rule lemmingd setup based on real development use

## Install

- Go: `go install github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/cmd/hamsterd@latest` and `go install github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/cmd/lemmingd@latest` (Go 1.26 or newer).
- Release archives for Linux, macOS, and Windows (amd64, arm64): https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/releases/latest
- Homebrew: `brew install --cask bopoha/tap/hamsterd bopoha/tap/lemmingd`
- Container (hamsterd shared cache): `ghcr.io/bopoha/hamsterd`, state volume `/var/lib/hamsterd`, configuration `/etc/hamsterd/config.json`; see [Run in a container](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/docs/hamsterd.md#run-in-a-container) and [Compose example](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/examples/docker-compose.yml)
- Fedora, EPEL 10, Amazon Linux 2023: `sudo dnf copr enable vorona/hamsterd && sudo dnf install hamsterd lemmingd`

## Key facts

- Both programs are forward proxies and listen only on loopback by default. lemmingd is a developer-workstation tool; hamsterd can also run as a shared cache for a trusted team network with `allow_remote_clients`, which refuses loopback, link-local, and metadata destinations and limits CONNECT to port 443 (configurable with `allowed_connect_ports`) but adds no authentication.
- Each program creates its own local certificate authority; private CA keys must never be published.
- hamsterd caches only eligible complete public GET responses and supports selective exact-host interception. Requests with credential-like headers bypass the cache; `default_ttl` applies only to responses with an ETag or Last-Modified validator.
- lemmingd intercepts only configured domains and routes matching path prefixes to configured local or explicitly allowed remote targets. Targets are `host:port`, `http://host:port`, or `https://host:port`; remote plain-HTTP targets require the explicit `http://` form.
- `lemmingd mcp` is an MCP server (stdio) for coding agents that controls a running lemmingd: tools `status`, `list_rules`, `test_route`, `recent_requests`, `add_rule`, `remove_rule`. It requires `"control_api": true` in lemmingd's config.json (off by default). Register it with `claude mcp add --scope user lemmingd -- lemmingd mcp`, `codex mcp add lemmingd -- lemmingd mcp`, `{"mcpServers": {"lemmingd": {"command": "lemmingd", "args": ["mcp"]}}}` (Claude Desktop, Cursor), or `{"servers": {"lemmingd": {"type": "stdio", "command": "lemmingd", "args": ["mcp"]}}}` (VS Code); GUI clients may need the absolute path of the binary. Per-client details: [Connect your MCP client](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/docs/lemmingd.md#connect-your-mcp-client). Rules added this way are stored in `rules.auto.json` (rules only, cannot change listen or remote-access settings); `lemmingd config show` prints the effective configuration and `lemmingd config merge` moves them into config.json. See [Control lemmingd from coding agents](https://github.com/BOPOHA/hamsterd/blob/main/docs/lemmingd.md#control-lemmingd-from-coding-agents-mcp).
- `lemmingd firefox URL` starts the proxy and launches a dedicated Firefox profile with profile-local proxy settings and CA trust; it requires Mozilla NSS `certutil` and does not change the default Firefox profile.
- Configuration format version is 1. The primary implementation language is Go.
- Build and verify with `make build`, `make test`, and `make vet`.

## Primary use cases

- Use hamsterd to avoid downloading the same Terraform providers, SDKs, browser binaries, compilers, public fixtures, or other cacheable build inputs on every clean build.
- Keep hamsterd outside ephemeral CI runners, containers, or development VMs so new environments can reuse earlier downloads.
- On a controlled development LAN, let several authorized machines reuse one hamsterd cache instead of maintaining a separate tool-specific cache on each machine. This requires explicit remote-client configuration, firewall controls, and CA distribution; hamsterd has no client authentication.
- Use lemmingd to serve a local `npm run dev` frontend and assets under a real QA or production-like HTTPS hostname while `/api/` continues to use the remote stack. Changes appear on refresh without a build or deployment.
- Preview a hosting migration before DNS cutover by routing one proxied browser to the candidate origin while a direct browser shows the current DNS-selected site at the same public URL.
- Launch an isolated, preconfigured Firefox session with `lemmingd firefox URL` for side-by-side direct and proxied browser testing.
- Reverse a lemmingd rule to exercise a local API implementation through the already-deployed frontend.
- Use separate browser-visible frontend and API hostnames to test a local API's real CORS behavior, or preserve one hostname to test same-origin cookies, redirects, OAuth callbacks, service workers, and Secure/SameSite behavior.
- Route selected assets or API calls to a local replacement, mock, or failure simulator while the rest of the application remains remote.

## Source layout

- `cmd/hamsterd/`: hamsterd executable
- `cmd/lemmingd/`: lemmingd executable
- `internal/`: shared and program-specific implementation packages
- `examples/`: example JSON configurations
- `docs/`: user guides, walkthroughs, and manual pages
- `packaging/`: RPM packaging
